description: A 32-bit pattern shifted along by a clock, in 10HP, with the chance of a bit changing under a knob, read out as sixteen pulses and two voltages

params.text: Chooses which bit a change lands on: the lowest bit, or a randomly picked one of the bits in use
Holds the pattern while it is pressed, or until the next press when its latch button is on, and the CV jack is ignored while it is held
Makes the lock button a toggle rather than a control that lasts while held
Chooses how the lock input is read: as a gate that locks while it is high, or as a trigger that flips the lock each time
Sets the chance that a clock pulse changes a bit at all, 0% fully counter-clockwise to 100% fully clockwise, at 50% in the centre
Attenuates and inverts the change-probability CV between -100% and +100%, and comes up at 0%
Sets what a changed bit becomes: the centre always flips it, counter-clockwise leans it towards 0 and clockwise towards 1
Attenuates and inverts the bit-probability CV between -100% and +100%, and comes up at 0%
Sets how many of the 32 bits the pattern runs round, 3 to 32, and 8 unless you move it
Attenuates and inverts the length CV between -100% and +100%, and comes up at 0%
Sets how wide a span the two voltage outputs cover, 0V to 10V
Attenuates and inverts the range CV between -100% and +100%, and comes up at 0%
Sets where that span falls, -10V to +10V, read as its bottom, middle or top according to the button beside it
Attenuates and inverts the anchor CV between -100% and +100%, and comes up at 0%
Steps the anchor knob's meaning through minimum, centre and maximum, with a light showing which
Clears the pattern, to random bits or to all zeros or all ones according to the switch beside it
Chooses what a reset writes: Rnd fills the pattern at random, 0's clears every bit, 1's sets every bit
Shifts the pattern one place and then gives the change probability its chance, exactly as a clock pulse does
Shifts the pattern one place without any chance of a bit changing, exactly as a rotate pulse does
Chooses what that pulse output carries: green for a gate held while its bit is 1, red for a trigger as the bit turns from 0 to 1

inputs.text: A high gate or a trigger freezes the pattern; a red mark beside the Lock label shows when it is held
Moves the change probability, 10V covering the knob's full travel at full trim
Moves the bit probability, 10V covering the knob's full travel at full trim
Moves the sequence length, each 0.345V adding one more step at full trim
Adds its voltage to the span after the trim knob
Adds its voltage to the anchor after the trim knob
A rising edge clears the pattern as the reset switch says
A rising edge gives the change probability its chance to flip a bit
A rising edge shifts the pattern one place; with the jack empty it reads the clock, so a clock alone both shifts and changes

outputs.text: Carries the lowest eight bits as a value from 0 to 255, mapped across the chosen span in 255 steps
Carries the lowest eight bits counted rather than weighted, so only how many are 1 matters, giving nine levels across the span
Carries the bit of that number as a gate or a trigger, according to the button beside it
Carries a gate or a trigger while both of the two named bits are 1 at once, which fires less often than a single bit does
Carries all sixteen pulses as sixteen channels, always as gates however the individual buttons are set

notes: the outputs are always built from eight bits: with the length above 8 only the lowest eight are used, and with it below 8 the pattern is repeated to fill eight
the 32-bit pattern is saved with the patch, so a sequence you like comes back when you load it
a clock and a rotate arriving in the same cycle rotate first and then take their chance on a bit change
menu: Lock-mode: Both change and rotate, Only bit-change, Only rotate — chooses what the lock freezes; by default the pattern keeps rotating while locked
Lock prevents reset — makes the lock block reset requests too, which it does not do unless you turn this on
Quantize mode — rounds the output to the nearest step of the size chosen, from a twelfth of a volt up to 5V, and is Off unless you set it
Clipping range — clamps every output to the range chosen, -12V to 12V unless you change it, and Off lets the output run to any voltage
Process quality: Audio, High, Balanced, Low, Very low — sets how often the module runs its algorithm, from every cycle down to every 256th; below Balanced a 1ms trigger can be missed
Gate-high detect-level — sets the voltage at which an incoming gate counts as high, 1V or more unless you change it
Gate-high output-level — sets the voltage a gate output carries while high, 10V unless you change it
Gate-low output-level — sets the voltage a gate output carries while low, 0V unless you change it
Trigger-high detect-level — sets the voltage at which an incoming trigger counts as high, 1V or more unless you change it
Trigger-low detect-level — sets the voltage an incoming trigger must fall back below before the next one is counted, under 0.1V unless you change it
Trigger-high output-level — sets the voltage a trigger pulse carries during its 1ms high phase, 10V unless you change it
Trigger-low output-level — sets the voltage a trigger output carries between pulses, 0V unless you change it
